title: Turkey Sausage & Sweet Potato Breakfast Skillet
subtitle: A leaner cast-iron breakfast built on turkey sausage, sweet potato, and eggs.
description: Turkey sausage and diced sweet potato crisp together in a cast-iron skillet, finished with eggs cracked over the top. It follows the hall's classic breakfast skillet format with a leaner sausage and a sweeter, more fiber-forward potato base.

steps.title: Par-cook the sweet potato
steps.instruction: Microwave diced sweet potato with a splash of water in a covered bowl until just tender. This cuts skillet time significantly and helps it crisp rather than steam.

steps.title: Build the crispy base
steps.instruction: Heat cast iron over medium-high with oil. Add sweet potato in a single layer; let it sit 3–4 minutes for color before tossing. Add onion and pepper and cook until softened.

steps.title: Brown the turkey sausage
steps.instruction: Push vegetables to one side. Add turkey sausage and break into crumbles, cooking 7–8 minutes until browned and 165°F. Fold everything together once cooked through.

steps.title: Make wells for the eggs
steps.instruction: Make shallow wells across the skillet and crack an egg into each well. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cover and finish
steps.instruction: Cover with a lid or inverted sheet pan over medium-low heat until egg whites are fully set and yolks are cooked to preference. Add cheese in the last minute to melt if using.

stationWorkflow: Par-cook sweet potato in the microwave first to save real skillet time.
Build the crispy base before adding sausage so both get proper browning.
Add eggs last so they finish exactly when the rest of the skillet is ready.
cleanupNotes: Deglaze the cast iron with hot water while still warm, then scrub once cool enough to handle.
Wipe down cutting boards immediately after raw sausage prep before eggs go anywhere near them.
leftovers: Reheat the potato-sausage base covered at 325°F for 10 minutes; fry fresh eggs rather than reheating set yolks.
Chop leftovers into a breakfast wrap with hot sauce for a fast next-shift meal.
